question: Blank vs zero DAF-grants cells: for the 248 FY2023 sponsors in IPS's sponsor list whose 'Grants from DAFs' cell is blank (no payout computed, so outside IPS's 9.7% median), read the same-FY Form 990 Schedule D Part I line 3(a) from the e-file XML and classify each as blank-filed, zero-filed or non-zero. Recompute IPS's median with the filed values
conclusion_affected: Whether IPS's 9.7% median is biased up by dropping blank-grants sponsors (counting them as 0% gives 7.7%)
rationale: IPS keeps 100 explicit zero-grant sponsors but drops 248 with a blank cell. Counting the blanks as zero moves the FY2023 median from 9.68% to 7.72%. The repo panel counts 132 zero-grant sponsor-years. Whether the blanks are true zeros is a filing question the XML can settle

question: Universe gap with IPS: the 172 FY2023 sponsors in IPS's list that have never been in the DAFRC panel (169 single-issue, median DAF assets $126k). Check whether their 990s report Schedule D Part I DAFs, and whether the DAFRC universe or the corrected totals miss them (an R4-type addition)
conclusion_affected: Completeness of the corrected sponsor universe; small single-issue sponsors in sponsor-median statistics
rationale: Every IPS-only sponsor is absent from the DAFRC panel in all of FY2019-24. They are small, so the dollar totals barely move, but they carry weight in any sponsor median (median rate 7.3%)

question: Account-level payout definition used by DAFRC's 2024 National Study (9% median, 3-year 2020-22): find the denominator (beginning, average or year-end balance plus grants) in the full report's methods or appendix, or in the DAFRC FAQ (johnsoncenter.org DAFRC-FAQ.pdf), so the residual in the bridge can be assigned to one denominator instead of being shown as a range
conclusion_affected: Size of the within-sponsor residual (6.6 to 12.5 points in FY2023)
rationale: The executive summary and the 2024 study slides state the 3-year window but not the denominator. The residual is 6.6 points against the IRS formula and 12.5 points against beginning assets

question: Sensitivity of the account-weighted median to its pivot sponsor: recompute the account-weighted median of sponsor payout rates without Fidelity Charitable, and with each top-10 sponsor by accounts left out in turn, FY2020-24
conclusion_affected: How robust the 'median account sits in a fast-paying national' step is
rationale: Ex processors, the account-weighted median is Fidelity's own rate in 4 of 5 years (FY2023: 15.6% IRS formula, 21.5% beginning assets). The step from median sponsor to median account therefore depends on one sponsor

question: Correct the repo's attribution of the 23.9% figure: several repository files call 23.9% both 'NPT's aggregate' (NPT 2024 DAF Report, FY2023) and the repo's own pooled FY2021-24 ex-processor gross payout (queue-net-payout-fidelity-outliers.md). Add a one-line disambiguation where both appear
rationale: The two 23.9% figures are different statistics on different samples and coincide by chance. IPS (p.14) quotes NPT's FY2023 23.9%. The repo pooled figure is a four-year sample of sponsors with itemised Schedule I
